protectedRevelations: Outfinitist seed design and final institutional proposals

scenes.title: Answers before judgment
scenes.viewerPurpose: Notice an answer sounding complete before you can question it Understand the book follows ideas gaining power
scenes.composition: A complete-looking answer arrives beside an unfinished question
addOrChange: Add a study table and remove oracle faces or supernatural light.

cues.narration: An answer can sound complete before we have learned how to question it.
cues.visualAction: The answer appears before the learner finishes the question.

cues.narration: The Schizoid and the Oracle asks how ideas gain power over people in the age of AI.
cues.visualAction: Keep the unfinished question visible as the book is named.

scenes.title: How ideas become authority
scenes.viewerPurpose: See a thought becoming a shared belief Question whether receiving words means understanding them
scenes.composition: A private notebook idea becomes a shared discussion
addOrChange: Add three listeners and a teaching circle without exotic ritual imagery.

cues.narration: It follows the path from a thought in one mind to a belief shared by many.
cues.visualAction: Move the notebook idea into a common discussion note.

cues.narration: Ancient teaching rituals and modern AI raise a similar question: does receiving an answer mean understanding it?
cues.visualAction: Show a learner asking what the received answer means.

scenes.title: The critic’s temptation
scenes.viewerPurpose: Understand the solitary thinker as a literary figure Notice who might use a persuasive idea for power
scenes.composition: An ordinary writer’s model enters a public decision
addOrChange: Keep faces non-clinical and add a decision desk separate from discussion.

cues.narration: Its solitary thinker is a character used to explore ideas, not a diagnosis.
cues.visualAction: Show the writer proposing a model without a diagnostic label.

cues.narration: The danger appears when a persuasive framework becomes useful to people seeking power.
cues.visualAction: An organizer carries the model toward authority as a participant questions it.

scenes.title: An ideology under review
scenes.viewerPurpose: Imagine beliefs that keep their leaders open to challenge Ask what followers must remain free to question
scenes.composition: Readers annotate a shared essay in front of its author
addOrChange: Add the listening author and retain the objection beside the claim.

cues.narration: Could people build a set of beliefs that still lets them question the people in charge?
cues.visualAction: A reader places a criticism beside the proposed belief.

cues.narration: What would an ideology look like if its followers could still challenge its creators?
cues.visualAction: The author’s essay stays open to that criticism.
